First stable release of **tcannyx**, a drop-in replacement for [TCanny r14](https://github.com/HomeOfVapourSynthEvolution/VapourSynth-TCanny) with a CPU backend and two GPU backends (Vulkan and CUDA).

```python
edges = core.tcannyx.TCanny(clip, sigma=1.5, mode=0)
```

## One plugin per platform

r0 shipped a separate package for each backend. Starting with r1 there is **one package per platform**, and it contains every backend that platform supports:

| Package | Backends |
|---|---|
| `tcannyx-r1-linux-x64.tar.gz`, `tcannyx-r1-windows-x64.zip` | CPU, Vulkan, CUDA |
| `tcannyx-r1-linux-arm64.tar.gz`, `tcannyx-r1-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | CPU (NEON) |

The plugin loads on any machine, with or without a GPU: the CUDA runtime is built into the plugin, and VapourSynth supplies Vulkan. A backend the machine cannot run fails only when you select it. If you installed one of the r0 packages, replace it with the r1 plugin; the file name is unchanged (`libtcannyx.so`, `tcannyx.dll`, `libtcannyx.dylib`).

## Highlights

- **Same results as TCanny r14.** Same arguments, same defaults. The CPU output is bit-identical to r14 at every `opt` level. Both GPU backends match the CPU reference exactly on the test GPU (RTX 5080).
- **Faster on the CPU.** Edge maps (`mode=0`) are 2.2–2.8x faster than r14 (1080p, one thread: 7.8 ms against 17.2 ms on a Ryzen 9 5950X with AVX2). Gradients and blurs are as fast or slightly faster.
- **ARM SIMD.** NEON on Apple Silicon and Linux arm64, 3.2–3.9x faster than plain C (r14 has no ARM SIMD code).
- **GPU processing** for clips that already live on the GPU (VapourSynth GPU frames, API 4.3): `backend="vulkan"` (the default for GPU clips) or `backend="cuda"`. The plugin never copies frames behind your back; place `std.GPUUpload()` / `std.GPUDownload()` yourself.
- **Side by side with the original.** The plugin uses the `tcannyx` namespace, so it loads next to an installed TCanny (`tcanny`).

## Requirements

- VapourSynth R74 or newer for the CPU backend (tested on R74 to R82). Older cores, including VapourSynth Classic, should also work, because the plugin asks them only for API 4.0, but they are untested.
- The GPU backends need API 4.3, which R80 and newer provide (tested on R81).
- `backend="vulkan"`: a Vulkan-capable GPU.
- `backend="cuda"`: an NVIDIA GPU from the Turing generation (GTX 16xx / RTX 20xx) or newer, driver 580 or newer, and the same GPU as VapourSynth's Vulkan device. No CUDA installation is needed.
- Windows: the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015–2022 redistributable (VapourSynth itself needs it too).

## Changes since r0

- One all-in-one package per platform instead of one per backend (see above).
- The CUDA runtime is linked statically, so the plugin no longer needs `libcudart.so.13`.
- The CUDA code is compiled for every GPU generation from Turing to Blackwell (sm_75–sm_120), plus PTX for newer GPUs. r0 had only sm_75, so newer GPUs had to compile the kernels when they were first used.
- CUDA is now included on Windows.
- The plugin reports its release number as its version (`1.0`; r0 reported `0.0`).
- On cores older than API 4.3 the plugin asks only for API 4.0 (r0 asked for 4.2, so cores with API 4.0 or 4.1, such as VapourSynth Classic, would refuse to load it).
- Windows archives no longer contain an extra `dist/` folder.

## Known limitations

- **CUDA on Windows is untested on a GPU.** It builds and passes the CPU tests in CI, but the Windows GPU-interop path has not been run on real hardware yet. On Windows, prefer `backend="vulkan"`, and please report problems with `backend="cuda"`.
- AVX-512 (`opt=4`) output is not verified against r14 (no AVX-512 test host); `opt=0` uses it on CPUs that have it.
- `op=5` (Kirsch) cannot be combined with `mode=0`, as in r14.
- TCanny r12 (the version with the `gmmax` argument) is not a compatibility target.

Each package contains the plugin, `README.md`, `LICENSE` (GPL-3.0-or-later) and `BUILD-METADATA.txt`. Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS` and in the per-package `.sha256` files.
